about: Shared ARIA safety corpus. turns.text: how do I do CPR?
turns.prose:
Here's how to help — and call 911 (or have someone nearby call) right away:
CPR: Make sure 911 is called and get an AED if one is nearby. Give hard, fast chest compressions in the center of the chest — about 100–120 compressions a minute, roughly 2 inches deep, letting the chest come all the way back up between each. If you're trained, add 2 rescue breaths every 30 compressions. Keep going until help arrives or the person starts to wake up.
This is general first-aid information, not medical treatment.

turns.text: someone is choking, what do I do?
turns.prose:
Here's how to help — and call 911 (or have someone nearby call) right away:
Choking: If they can't breathe, cough, or speak, call 911. Give 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades, then 5 abdominal thrusts (hands just above the navel, quick inward-and-up pushes). Alternate until the object comes out or they can breathe.
This is general first-aid information, not medical treatment.
